1.label: Message Passing Neural Networks for Quantum Chemistry (QM9)
1.gloss: Message-passing and equivariant graph neural networks (e.g. Message Passing Neural Network, SE(3)-Transformer) with components such as Set2Set readout and GRU update, evaluated on QM9.

2.label: Crystal Graph Networks for Material Property and Phonon Prediction
2.gloss: Graph neural network methods (e.g. ALIGNN, Allegro) on crystal graph representations predicting material properties such as band gap and formation energy, including full phonon band structure prediction, with data from Materials Project.

3.label: Crystal-Graph Attention Networks (CGAT) for Stability Screening
3.gloss: The Crystal-Graph Attention Network series (CGAT, DCGAT-2) used for convex hull distance prediction and screening tasks such as hard material discovery and high-Tc superconductor identification.

4.label: Graph-Network Potentials and Property Models (broad)
4.gloss: A broad catch-all group of graph-network models (e.g. Crystal Hamiltonian Graph neural Network, Euclidean neural networks, MEGNet) for fast energy/force/stress and property prediction, applied to tasks such as grain-boundary energy calculation and martensitic phase transition modeling.

5.label: Atomic Cluster Expansion for Vectorial and Tensorial Properties
5.gloss: Extension of the Atomic Cluster Expansion to scalar, vectorial and tensorial properties with magnetic and charge degrees of freedom, using Clebsch-Gordan coupling and analytic gradient evaluation for forces and torques.
entities: Magnetic and Charge Degrees of Freedom

6.label: Energy RMSE on Acetylacetone
6.gloss: Energy RMSE (meV) evaluation on the acetylacetone dataset.

7.label: EquiformerV2: Equivariant Transformer on OC20/OC22
7.gloss: EquiformerV2, an equivariant Transformer using equivariant graph attention and attention re-normalization, evaluated on OC20 and OC22 energy and force prediction.

8.label: Molecular and Elemental Benchmark Sets with Energy/Force Errors
8.gloss: Benchmark datasets such as Aspirin (MD-17) and Benzene, together with error and cost metrics such as Energy MAE, force MAE and wall-clock time.

9.label: Interatomic Potentials on OMol25: Transformers and Learned Equivariance
9.gloss: Machine-learned interatomic potentials evaluated on OMol25, including Transformer-based Inter-Atomic Potentials, TransAug and GemNet-OC, with components such as continuous-filter convolution and a contrastive latent equivariance loss.

10.label: Machine Learning for Multiscale Computational Modeling: Challenges
10.gloss: Perspective on machine learning for multiscale modeling (neural operators, transfer learning, meta-learning) in computational mechanics and fluid mechanics, naming problems such as data scarcity and model interpretability.

11.label: SevenNet: Parallel GNN Potentials for Large-Scale MD
11.gloss: The SevenNet package and a spatial decomposition scheme for GNN-IPs enabling multi-GPU parallelization of large-scale MD, applied to SiO2 and amorphous Si3N4.

12.label: MACE: Higher-Order Equivariant Message Passing
12.gloss: MACE, an equivariant message passing network with higher-order many-body messages, Bessel radial basis functions and loop tensor contraction, targeting data-efficiency and scalability.

13.label: Energy-Conserving vs Unconstrained Equivariant Potentials
13.gloss: E(3)-equivariant convolution potentials with energy-conserving force computation, contrasted with unconstrained models that give energy-non-conserving force predictions.

14.label: Long-Range Electrostatics and Charge Equilibration in MLIPs
14.gloss: Long-range electrostatic modeling in MLIPs via charge equilibration (CELLI), Latent Ewald Summation and Euclidean Fast Attention, with biased data splitting to test chemical space generalization on QMOF and ODAC25.

15.label: Universal MLIP Benchmark Datasets (LAMBench, MADBench, SPICE)
15.gloss: Benchmark datasets for universal MLIPs such as LAMBench, MADBench, OC20-NEB and SPICE, with metrics including DAF and MAE E.

16.label: Benchmarking Universal MLIPs for NEB Migration Barriers
16.gloss: An MLIP-NEB benchmarking workflow assessing MLIPs such as CHGNet, M3GNet and MACE-MP-0 on migration barriers for high-throughput ionic conductor screening.

17.label: DeePMD-kit v2 and Deep Potential Models for Ionic Diffusion
17.gloss: The DeePMD-kit v2 software package with Deep Potential models (DeepPot-SE, DPA-1) and DP-GEN, applied to diffusion coefficient and activation energy estimation in materials such as LGPS, LLZO and NASICON.

18.label: Training Datasets for ML Interatomic Potentials (MPtrj, MatPES, OMat24)
18.gloss: Training datasets and dataset-generation workflows for ML interatomic potentials (MPtrj, MatPES, OMat24, Alexandria) using stratified sampling, BIRCH clustering and DeNS denoising.

19.label: Flow-Matching Models for Atomistic Dynamics (LiFlow)
19.gloss: Flow Matching models such as LiFlow, built from a Propagator and a Corrector with a modified PaiNN flow approximator and an adaptive Maxwell–Boltzmann prior.

20.label: Automatminer: AutoML for Materials Property Prediction on Matbench
20.gloss: Automatminer, an AutoML pipeline with automated feature generation and automated model selection for materials property prediction, benchmarked on the Matbench test suite.

21.label: Matbench Discovery: Benchmarking Stable-Crystal Prediction
21.gloss: Matbench Discovery, benchmarking models such as CGCNN, MEGNet, Equiformer and BOWSR on the WBM test set for thermodynamic stability classification and convex-hull distance regression.

22.label: AFLOW High-Throughput DFT Framework and Standard
22.gloss: The AFLOW framework and standard for high-throughput DFT calculations, covering phonon dispersion, convex-hull phase diagram construction and interstitial site discovery.

23.label: DeepH-E3: Equivariant DFT Hamiltonians with Spin-Orbit Coupling
23.gloss: DeepH-E3, an E(3)-equivariant neural network for DFT Hamiltonian learning including strong spin-orbit coupling, evaluated on MoS2 and graphene.

24.label: Equivariant Hamiltonian Learning for Magnetic and Twisted Materials
24.gloss: A deep equivariant neural network method for predicting DFT Hamiltonian matrices of magnetic and moiré-twisted materials, tested on Moiré-twisted bilayer CrI3, NiBr2 spin-spiral and twisted bilayer graphene.

25.label: Universal Potentials, Active Learning and Phase-Field Models (broad)
25.gloss: A broad catch-all group spanning pretrained universal potentials (CHGNet, M3GNet), Deep Potential molecular dynamics, active learning workflows and Allen–Cahn / Cahn–Hilliard phase field models.

26.label: ConvLSTM Prediction of Brittle Fracture from MD
26.gloss: A ConvLSTM-based fracture prediction model trained on MD simulation data to predict crack paths and fracture toughness, including bicrystal and gradient-orientation cases.
entities: Fracture pattern prediction from MD simulations

27.label: Future Directions: Materials Datasets, Benchmarks and Foundation Models
27.gloss: Future-work topics from dataset, benchmark and survey papers (e.g. Matbench Discovery, OMat24, JARVIS), such as continuous expansion of JARVIS datasets and larger, higher-quality PES datasets.

28.label: Interpretable Melting Temperature Prediction for Inorganic Compounds
28.gloss: Interpretable, cluster-based models (SISSO, Extreme Gradient Boosting, SHAP analysis) for melting temperature prediction of binary inorganic compounds from elemental and DFT-derived features.

29.label: Future Directions: ML Potentials, Electronic Structure and Multiscale AI
29.gloss: Future-work topics on machine-learning interatomic potentials, AI-accelerated electronic structure prediction and data-driven multiscale modeling, alongside the Universal HamGNN Hamiltonian model.

30.label: Gaussian Approximation Potential for Silicon
30.gloss: A Gaussian Approximation Potential (GAP) for silicon built with the SOAP kernel, sparse Gaussian process regression and CUR matrix decomposition, with uncertainty quantification.

31.label: Cross-Domain Benchmarks and Metrics for MLIPs
31.gloss: Benchmark datasets and metrics for evaluating MLIPs across domains such as catalysis (AdsorbML), the CSP Blind Test and elasticity, with metrics like Energy/Atom MAE and MAE_Kbulk.

32.label: Carbon Potentials and Universal Atomistic Models (broad)
32.gloss: A broad catch-all group combining interatomic potentials for carbon (Tersoff, REBO, Gaussian approximation potentials with SOAP descriptors) with universal models such as Orb-v3 and Universal Models for Atoms.

33.label: Heuristic + ML Formation-Energy Screening of Ternary Compounds (OQMD)
33.gloss: A combined heuristic-ML pipeline (decision-tree regression) predicting ternary formation energies with the OQMD, applied to screening Li-ion battery anodes, HF-scavenging cathode coatings and Mg-based LPSO precipitates.

34.label: Task Mentions (catch-all)
34.gloss: A catch-all group consisting only of task-type nodes, e.g. AIMD simulations, activation energy estimation and AdsorbML adsorption energy calculation.

35.label: Descriptor-Based Screening of Superionic Conductors
35.gloss: Screening of solid-state ionic conductors with free-volume descriptors, the frozen framework approximation and ML-IAPs (CHGNet, M3GNet), combined via descriptor fusion and CatBoost classification models.

36.label: Future Directions: Accelerated Simulation of Solid-State Electrolytes
36.gloss: Future-work topics on extending LiFlow and flow-matching models, integrating universal MLIPs and high-throughput screening for ionic transport in solid-state electrolytes.

37.label: D4FT: Stochastic-Gradient KS-DFT
37.gloss: D4FT, a GPU-accelerated reformulation of KS-DFT that replaces slow self-consistent field convergence with mini-batch stochastic gradient descent over a neural local scaling basis, using automatic differentiation via JAX.

38.label: JARVIS Integrated Materials Design Infrastructure
38.gloss: The JARVIS integrated materials design infrastructure (JARVIS-DFT, JARVIS-FF, CFID descriptors) for high-throughput DFT property calculation, force-field benchmarking and machine-learning property prediction.

39.label: LLM Agents and Foundation Models for Materials Discovery
39.gloss: LLM-agent frameworks and foundation models (CLIP, BERT) for accelerated materials discovery, covering hypothesis generation, experimental plan generation and human-in-the-loop workflows.

40.label: Future Directions: Universal Models for Atoms at Scale (Orb-v3, UMA)
40.gloss: Future-work topics from the Orb-v3 and UMA papers, such as uniting universality and scalability in MLIPs and generalization across chemical domains.
entities: Uniting universality and scalability in MLIPs
